title: Branching, merging and conflicts
text: Now interesting case. Two branches edit row: part catches people . Conflicts DoltLite never durable — exist inside transaction produced . merge run autocommit mode, get default, rolled back full moment conflicts: Nothing left behind inspect: actually work conflict, put merge transaction: per-table view carries base_, our_ their_ columns, can see three sides : Resolve taking one side wholesale, editing rows directly resolving: Note dolt_commit() also ended SQL transaction, nothing left DBI::dbCommit() : commit refused conflict remains, accidentally record half-merged state.
code: dolt_checkout(con, "regional", create = TRUE) DBI::dbExecute(con, "UPDATE sites SET region = 'County Cork' WHERE id = 1") #> [1] 1 dolt_commit(con, "Use full county names")  dolt_checkout(con, "main") DBI::dbExecute(con, "UPDATE sites SET region = 'CORK' WHERE id = 1") #> [1] 1 dolt_commit(con, "Normalise regions to upper case") dolt_merge(con, "regional") #> Error in `dbBind()`: #> ! cannot merge: conflicts detected, autocommit transaction rolled back. Run the merge inside BEGIN/COMMIT to inspect dolt_conflicts and dolt_schema_conflicts, resolve with dolt_conflicts_resolve(), then commit with dolt_commit(). Conflicts are never committed as conflicts nrow(dolt_conflicts(con)) #> [1] 0 DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT region FROM sites WHERE id = 1") #>   region #> 1   CORK DBI::dbBegin(con) dolt_merge(con, "regional") #> [1] "Merge has 1 conflict(s). Resolve and then commit with dolt_commit." dolt_conflicts(con) #>   table num_conflicts #> 1 sites             1 detail <- dolt_conflicts_table(con, "sites") detail[, grep("region|dolt_conflict_id", names(detail), value = TRUE)] #>   base_region our_region their_region dolt_conflict_id #> 1        Cork       CORK  County Cork              1:0 dolt_conflicts_resolve(con, "ours") nrow(dolt_conflicts(con)) #> [1] 0  dolt_commit(con, "Merge regional, keeping upper-case regions") DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT region FROM sites WHERE id = 1") #>   region #> 1   CORK DBI::dbCommit(con) #> Error: #> ! no transaction is open on this connection
